One atomic write: a single checkin or a whole changeset, recorded as a git commit on a branch. `id` is the git
commit id, so a commit can be fetched with a unique abbreviation of at least 4 digits.

author_current.description:
The author's account name now, when it was renamed after the commit (decision #986); `author.name` stays as
written because the commit id covers it.

oneOf.description: The author's public identity (the current name's account when renamed); absent when no active account holds it.

authored_at.description: The author time, in whole seconds; its timezone is `author.offset_minutes`. Absent from servers that predate it.

changeset.description: Set when the commit was made as a changeset.

created_at.description: The committer time, in whole seconds.

message.description: The message decoded lossily; a commit's exact bytes are never altered.

parents.description: Empty for the first commit of the repository, otherwise the commit it was made on top of.

revisions.description: The revisions the commit made, ordered by path.

signature.description: The commit's `gpgsig` header, when it is signed.

tree.description: The id of the root git tree of the repository as of this commit.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next, older page; null on the last page.

CompareChange.description: A path the head changes relative to the merge base.

name.description: Git ref rules apply: no spaces, none of `~ ^ : ? * [ \`, no `..`.

start.description: A branch name, or a commit id or abbreviation of at least 4 digits; the default branch's head if omitted.

hours.description: How long the invitation can be used, in hours.

name.description: Normalised to a canonical name (trimmed, spaces become `-`, lowercased); shares the namespace with user names: 2 to 39 letters, digits, `-` or `_`, not reserved. The typed form becomes the display name when it differs.

base.description: The branch to merge into; the default branch if omitted.

allow_private_forks.description: Whether people who can read the repository may fork it while it is private. Defaults to `false`.

description.description: One line, at most 350 characters; blank means none.

max_locks_per_user.description: Locks one user may hold; defaults to the server's. A limit in the repository's policy file overrides it.

name.description: Normalised to a canonical name (trimmed, spaces become `-`, lowercased): 1 to 100 letters, digits, `-`, `_` or `.`, starting with a letter or digit and not ending in `.`.

owner.description:
The namespace to create it in: the caller's own account name, or an organization whose repository-creation
policy lets them. Defaults to the caller.

oneOf.description:
The starter policy's `[meta] default`: whether paths no entry covers are `shared` or `exclusive`. Defaults to
`shared`; ignored when `starter_policy` is `false`.

starter_policy.description:
Defaults to `true`: the first commit holds `.pyn/pyn.toml` with the starter policy (shared by default, exclusive
rules for object and binary files). `false` leaves the repository empty, under the server's initial policy.

topics.description: At most 20 topics of 1 to 50 lowercase letters, digits or `-`; uppercase is lowered and repeats dropped.

oneOf.description: Defaults to `private`.

website.description: An http or https link; blank means none.

email.description: Where to send the code; used only when a mailer is configured, and stored only to tell invitations apart.

expires_in_days.description: Days the code works, 1 to 90; 7 when left out.

allowed_sources.description:
Addresses or CIDR blocks (`192.0.2.7`, `10.0.0.0/8`, `2001:db8::/32`) the credential may be used from, at most 64.
Omit or leave empty to allow any address.

expires_at.description: The credential is refused from this instant on; it must be in the future. Omit for no expiry.

name.description: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`; unique, and never reused after revocation.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Requests per minute this credential may make, at least 1. Omit to use the server default.

message.description: An optional note kept with the tag.

name.description: Git ref rules apply: no spaces, none of `~ ^ : ? * [ \`, no `..`.

target.description: A branch or tag name, or a commit id or abbreviation of at least 4 digits; the default branch's head if omitted.

description.description: At most 500 characters; defaults to empty.

name.description: 1 to 100 characters; defaults to the slug.

slug.description: 1 to 39 lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, starting with a letter or digit; unique in the organization.

expires_at.description: When the token expires; without it and without `never` the token lasts 30 days.

owner.description: The resource owner: the caller's own account or an organization they belong to. Defaults to the caller.

permissions.description:
Metadata read is implied for `all` and `selected`, which need at least one repository permission; `public`
takes no repository permissions. Organization and account permissions go with any repository access.

event_types.description:
Event types to deliver, such as `repository.created`; empty or left out means every type. An unknown type is
refused with `400 invalid_request`.

url.description: `https` only (`http` when the operator allows it), no user name or password, no fragment, at most 2048 bytes.

code.description: Give this to the person being invited. Shown once and never stored.
Give this to the person being invited, as `pyn register <name> --invite <code>` or in the sign-up form. Shown once.

emailed.description: The message was handed to a configured mailer; false when no address was given or no mailer is on.

secret.description: Presented as a bearer credential. Shown once and never stored.

token.description: The token to present as a bearer credential. Shown once and never stored.

secret.description: The signing secret: `whsec_` and 64 hex characters. Shown once and never returned again.

CreationEffect.description: Whether a creation rule permits or forbids.

CreationRuleInfo.description: A subject holds at most one rule per effect. A matching `deny` beats any `allow`.

subject.description: The team slug, user name, or organization role (`owner` or `member`).

CreationScope.description: Which repository visibilities a rule or policy covers.

CreationSubjectKind.description: What a creation rule's subject names.

DeleteOwnAccountRequest.description: Schedules the deletion of the signed-in account after the recovery window.

password.description: The account's password, entered again. An account with no password needs a web session and may leave it empty.

DeletionBlockers.description: What stops an account from being deleted until it is transferred or deleted.

organizations.description: Organizations the account is the only owner of.

binary.description: A binary file has no hunks.

file_mode.description: The git file mode of the new side (of the old side for a deletion).

oneOf.description: The live lock on the path, whoever holds it.

mode.description: The path's mode under the repository's policy.

old_content.description: Git blob ids of the two sides; absent where the path does not exist.

oneOf.description: The previous git file mode, when it changed.

old_path.description: The previous path of a renamed file.

too_large.description: The file, or the diff as a whole, is over the size limits: no hunks, and `additions` and `deletions` are 0.

hidden_after.description: Unchanged lines after the last hunk to the end of the file; 0 on every other hunk.

hidden_before.description: Unchanged lines between the previous hunk (or the start of the file) and this one; `/lines` loads them.

new_no.description: Line number in the new file; absent on a deleted line.

no_newline.description: The file's last line on this side has no newline.

old_no.description: Line number in the old file; absent on an added line.

reason.description: Shown to administrators; not to the account holder.

EmailFailure.description: A refused send. The error never carries a recipient address or a credential.

oneOf.description: The newest send the mailer refused since the server started; null when none failed.

last_sent_at.description: When a message last went out since the server started; null when none has.

verification.description: Whether sign-up must confirm the address (`PYN_EMAIL_VERIFICATION`, on by default when a mailer is set).

ErrorBody.description: Body of every non-2xx response; `code` is stable and machine-readable.

oneOf.description: What blocks the account's deletion; present only with `account_owns_resources`.

Event.description:

`*Data` for each known type. A receiver ignores types it does not know.

id.description: Unique per event; a redelivery keeps it.

type.description:
The event type, a dotted name such as `repository.created`. An open set: new types are added without a
new `version`.

ExternalIdentityInfo.description: A provider identity linked to an account.

email.description: The address the provider last gave, if it vouched for one.

name.description: What to call it on the sign-in button.

sign_in_url.description: Send the browser here (a full page navigation, with an optional `return_to` path) to start signing in.

data.description: Base64 of the commit's body, as in a push.

pointers.description: The revisions the commit's pointer cache records: what it wrote and what a merge adopted, ordered by path.

trees.description: The trees the commit adds against its first parent, as in a push.

head.description: The branch's head when the fetch started; null for a branch with no commit.

branches.description: The branches to fetch; every branch if empty. Ignored when `cursor` is given.

haves.description: Commits the client already has, normally its branch heads; ids the repository does not know are ignored.

limit.description: Commits per page; the server's default and cap apply when omitted or larger.

next.description: Opaque; send it as `cursor` for the next page. Absent on the last page.

file_mode.description: The head revision's git file mode; `100644` when there is no revision.

revision.description: Head revision; absent if the path is locked but has no revision yet.

FileLines.description: A range of the lines of a file at a revision.

lines.description: Lines without their newlines; empty past the end of the file.

revision.description: The path's revision number at that commit.

start.description: The number of the first line in `lines`, counting from 1.

FileMode.description: Git's file mode for a file: regular, executable or symbolic link (whose content is the link target).

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

FolderUsage.description: Distinct stored bytes of one top-level folder.

files.description: Paths with a revision under the folder.

folder.description: The top-level folder; empty for the files at the root.

reason.description: Why the lock is being removed; required and recorded in the audit log.

owner.description:

visibility. Defaults to the caller.

FreezeRequest.description: Freezes an owner, or replaces the reason and time of a freeze already in force.

reason.description: Shown to the owner's members: 1 to 512 bytes.

FreshCheck.description: Until when the calling credential may do sensitive actions without another second-factor check.

HistoryAuthors.description: The accounts that wrote revisions on a branch, for a history author filter.

authors.description: Account names as written in the revisions (what `author` filters on), sorted; a renamed account's older revisions keep its old name.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next page (the next newer one with `path`, the next older one without); null on the last page.

revisions.description: With `path`: that path's revisions, oldest first. Without: newest first.

LanguageShare.description: One programming language's share of a repository, detected from file names.

name.description: A display name such as `Rust` or `C++`.

LimitKind.description: Which limit an owner ran into.

Limits.description: Limits on one owner. Every limit is opt-in: a null field is unlimited.

members.description: Members an organization may have; always null for a user.

storage_bytes.description: Bytes of distinct content across the owner's repositories.

LimitsListing.description: The server default and every owner that has limits of its own.

defaults.description: Applies to owners with nothing of their own; all null unless the operator configures it.

oneOf.description: The owner's public identity; absent when the account is gone or not active.

LockAcquiredData.description: `lock.acquired`: a path was locked, including when a lapsed lease was taken over. A renewal raises nothing.

acting_admin.description: The administrator who acted as `holder` in an access session; absent otherwise.

LockExpiredData.description: `lock.expired`: a lease had lapsed when the path was locked again; observed lazily, not at the expiry instant.

LockForcedData.description: `lock.forced`: a live lock was removed without its holder, by a forced unlock or a policy change.

acting_admin.description: The administrator who acted as `actor` in an access session; absent otherwise.

acting_admin.description: The administrator who acted as `holder` in an access session; absent otherwise.

reason.description: `checkin` when a revision of the path consumed the lock; null for an explicit release.

LockStreamEvent.description: One lock change in a repository's stream.

cursor.description: Resume after this event by passing it as `after`.

event.description: The same envelope a webhook delivers: `lock.acquired`, `lock.released`, `lock.expired` or `lock.forced`.

LockStreamPage.description: A page of a repository's lock changes, oldest first.

cursor.description:
Pass it as `after` to get what follows this page. It is the position of the last event returned, or of the
request when none was; without `after` it is the position of now and `events` is empty.

LockableDisagreement.description: A path whose `lockable` attribute and policy mode disagree.

code.description:
The authenticator-app code (or a recovery code) of an account with a second factor. Without it such an
account gets `401 second_factor_required` after a right password.

remember.description:
`POST /v1/session` only: stay signed in for `PYN_SESSION_REMEMBER_DAYS` instead of `PYN_SESSION_DAYS`.
Absent or false keeps the usual lifetime.

MailerKind.description: Which mailer the server sends with. Never carries a host or a credential.

Me.description: The caller and what they may do in one repository.

oneOf.description: The member's public identity; absent when the account is not active.

role.description: The effective role: the highest of the direct grant, team grants and organization ownership.

MemberCreation.description: What members may create when no rule applies.

MemberSource.description: What decides a member's effective role.

MergeChange.description: A path the merge changes in the target, with the content it ends up with.

oneOf.description: The versions to merge line by line, present only when no revision holds the result.

MergeConversion.description: The conversion of a path to exclusive that a merge conflict met, and the shared version it stranded.

diverged_revision.description: The diverged shared revision the conversion stranded, with its author and time.

policy_revision.description: The policy revision in force at the conversion.

revision.description: The conversion revision, the first of the path's exclusive line.

MergeFastForward.description: Whether a merge may or must fast-forward.

MergeInputs.description: The versions a path's merge is made from; a side is null where the path does not exist.

base_inline.description: The base's bytes, base64, when no revision holds it (a virtual base), so a client can still merge against it.

expect_head.description: The head branch's commit the caller saw.

expect_target.description: The base branch's commit the caller saw; a different head is `409 merge_stale`.

oneOf.description: `allow` (the default), `never` or `only`, as for a merge.

message.description: The merge commit's message; `Merge pull request #N from <head>` if omitted.

MergeReport.description: What a merge does, or did.

bases.description: The merge base commits; more than one means a criss-cross history.

changes.description: Paths whose content changes in the target, ordered by path.

commit.description: The commit the merge wrote; null for a preview and for an up-to-date merge.

stranded.description:
Shared versions on other branches that the policy file a merge into the default branch brought stranded;
empty for a preview and for every other merge.

target_commit.description: The target's head the merge was computed on; null for a branch with no commits.

virtual_base.description: True when the bases were merged into a virtual one.

MergeRequest.description: A source (a branch, or a commit) merged into a target branch.

expect_target.description: The commit the caller saw as the target's head; if the branch has moved the answer is `merge_stale`.

message.description: The merge commit's message; `Merge branch '<source>' into <target>` if omitted.

resolutions.description: The content chosen for each conflicted path (and optionally for a path that merged cleanly).

source.description: A branch name, or a commit id or abbreviation of at least 4 digits.

target.description: The branch that moves; the default branch if omitted.

MergeResolution.description: The content chosen for one path of a merge: an uploaded object, by its blob id.

oneOf.description: Git's file mode of the content; regular if omitted.

MergeSide.description: One version of a path in a merge.

content.description: The git blob id of the content.

revision.description: The revision that holds this version; null for the virtual base of a criss-cross merge.

MissingObjectsRequest.description: Chunk digests to check against the server's object store.

hashes.description: SHA-256 hex of each chunk's bytes; at most 10000.

missing.description: The digests from the request that the server does not store.

MyLock.description: A live lock the caller holds, with the repository it is in.

Notice.description: A message for the account, shown by the web app until dismissed.

kind.description: `two_factor_reset`: an administrator reset the account's second factors.

OidcLink.description: Where to send the browser to link the provider to the signed-in account.

OrgInfo.description: An organization: a namespace that owns repositories.

oneOf.description: The caller's standing in it (`owner` or `member`); absent when they have none.

OrgInvitation.description: A pending offer of organization membership. It becomes a membership with `role` when `user` accepts.

expires_at.description: After this the invitation is gone and cannot be accepted.

oneOf.description: The member's public identity; absent when the account is not active.

OrgProfile.description: What an organization shows about itself.

avatar_url.description: `/v1/orgs/{org}/avatar?v=` and the start of the image's hash; null when there is no avatar.

description.description: At most 256 characters; null when unset.

display_name.description: 1 to 80 characters, shown beside the name; null when unset.

url.description: An http or https website link of at most 200 characters, without credentials; null when unset.

OrgRole.description: A person's standing in an organization.

OrgSettingsInfo.description: An organization's repository defaults; a field that is absent or null is not set by the organization.

org_id.description: The deleted organization's id, never issued again.

own.description: Limits set for this owner alone; a null field follows the server default.

OwnerUsage.description: What an owner uses against its limits.

backup_state.description: The passkey is currently synced or backed up.

sign_count.description: The signature counter last seen; 0 for authenticators that keep none.

transports.description: How the authenticator reaches the browser (`usb`, `nfc`, `ble`, `internal`, `hybrid`), as the browser reported.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use recovery codes, shown only now, and only with the account's first second factor.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

display_name.description: At most 64 characters, trimmed, no control characters.

RepoDiff.description: The changes of a head against a base, with line hunks.

base.description: The base as named in the request (the default branch when none was given).

from_commit.description: The commit the changes are measured from: the merge base, or the base for a direct diff.

allow_private_forks.description: Whether people who can read this private repository may fork it; a public one can always be forked.

description.description: One line of plain text for the About block; null when unset.

exclusive_read_only.description:
Whether exclusive files are read-only in a work tree until their lock is held: the policy file's
`meta.exclusive_read_only`, else the owning organization's setting, else on.

fork_count.description: How many repositories were forked from this one, whoever owns them and whatever their visibility.

oneOf.description:
The repository this one was forked from; null for an original, when the source was deleted, and when the
caller cannot see the source.

id.description: Stable, never reused and unchanged by a rename; a deleted repository's id is never issued again.

language.description: The first entry of `languages`; null when there is none.

languages.description:
Bytes of each programming language at the head of the default branch, largest first; empty for an empty
repository or one with no recognised source files. A client computes percentages from `bytes`.

lease_hours.description: How long a lock lasts before it expires unless renewed.

max_locks_per_user.description:
Locks one user may hold in the repository: the policy file's `meta.max_locks_per_user` if it sets one, else
the repository setting, else the server default.

max_locks_per_user_setting.description: The repository setting alone; absent when it follows the server default. Not in force while the policy file sets one.

max_locks_set_by_policy.description: True when `.pyn/pyn.toml` sets the limit; the setting then cannot be changed.

owner_id.description: The id of `owner`, a user or an organization.

oneOf.description: The owning organization's public identity (its avatar); absent when a user owns the repository.
The caller's role in the repository; absent when they have none.

star_count.description: How many accounts starred the repository. Anyone who can read the repository sees it, private ones included.

starred.description: Whether the caller starred it; false for a signed-out caller.

topics.description: Lowercase labels set by the owner, in their order; empty when none.

updated_at.description: When the newest commit of the default branch was made; null for an empty repository.

watcher_count.description: How many accounts watch the repository at `all` or `locks`. Anyone who can read the repository sees it.

oneOf.description: The caller's watch level; null when they chose none, and for a signed-out caller.

website.description: An http or https link for the About block; null when unset.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

RepoPolicyInfo.description: An organization's repository-creation policy. Owners can always create repositories and are not listed in it.

member_creation.description: What members may create when no rule applies; `none` (owners only) is the default.

rules.description: Ordered by kind, subject, then effect.

files.description: Paths with at least one revision on the default branch.

locks.description: Live locks with their holders, ordered by path.

updated_at.description: Time of the newest revision; absent for an empty repository.

RepoTeam.description: A team of the owning organization and its role in a repository.

team_id.description: Stable id of the team; never reused after a delete.

lfs_bytes.description: Bytes of LFS objects. The storage cap applies to `stored_bytes` plus this.

storage_cap.description: The repository's own storage cap in bytes; null when it has none.

RepoUsageBreakdown.description:
Where a repository's stored bytes sit. Content shared by several folders or paths counts in each, so their sums
can pass `stored_bytes`.

lfs_bytes.description: Bytes of the repository's LFS objects, not part of the folders and paths.

stored_bytes.description: Distinct bytes in the whole repository, each content once.

RepositoryAccess.description: Which repositories of the token's owner it reaches.

mode.description:
`public` (none beyond the public repositories every token can read), `all` (every repository the owner
has now and later) or `selected` (only `repos`).

repos.description: `owner/name` of each selected repository, all owned by the token's owner; empty unless `selected`.

repo_id.description: The deleted repository's id, never issued again.

RepositoryRenamedData.description: `repository.renamed`: the name changed; the owner never does.

repo_id.description: Unchanged by the rename: re-key on it.

RepositoryStorageCapChangedData.description: `repository.storage_cap_changed`: a repository's own storage cap was set or removed; `storage_cap` is the result.

storage_cap.description: Bytes the repository may store; null when it has no cap of its own.

base_revision.description: The current head the caller is looking at; must still be the head.

branch.description: The branch the restore is committed on; the default branch if omitted.

confirm.description: `<path>@r<base_revision>`, confirming the caller knows which head is being replaced.

revision.description: The older revision whose content becomes the new head.

author_current.description:
The author's name now, when the account was renamed after writing this revision (decision #986). `author`
stays as written because the hash covers it; show this one.

oneOf.description: The structured author the v2 hash covers; absent for a v1 revision, whose hash predates it.
The author's public identity (the current name's account when renamed); absent when no active account holds it.

base.description:
The revision this one was based on, the committing branch's revision of the path; absent when the branch had
none. Not covered by `hash`; `pyn verify` checks that it names an older revision of the path.

changeset.description: Shared by the revisions checked in together as one changeset; absent for a single-path checkin.

commit.description: The id of the commit this revision belongs to; see `Commit`.

content.description: The content's git blob id (SHA-256 hex of `blob <len>\0` followed by the content).

deleted.description:
The revision removes the path from its branch; `content` and `file_mode` are those of the version removed.
Its `hash_version` is 3.

file_mode.description: The git file mode of the content.

hash.description: SHA-256 hex over the revision's canonical encoding, by `hash_version` (docs/concepts/integrity.md).

hash_version.description: The encoding `hash` uses: 1 or 2. Version 2 requires `author_identity`, version 1 forbids it.

legacy_content.description:
The content string this revision's `hash` covers, when it differs from `content`: revisions that predate blob
ids, whose hash covers the SHA-256 hex of the bare content.

oneOf.description: The path's mode when the revision was made; absent for revisions that predate recording it.

previous.description: The hash of the path's previous revision by number; absent for the first.

restored_from.description: Set when this revision restored the content of an earlier one.

stranded.description:
Only in the response to checking in or restoring `.pyn/pyn.toml` on the default branch: the diverged shared
versions on other branches that the change stranded. Empty, and omitted, everywhere else.

Role.description: A role in a repository, lowest to highest.

secret.description: The new signing secret. Shown once and never returned again.

ServerAccess.description: The server's access mode, as read and as changed by an administrator.

ServerCapabilities.description: What this server supports beyond the base API; a client checks it before it relies on a newer route.

local_commits.description: The server accepts pushed commits and serves fetches (`/push`, `/fetch`), so a client may keep commits locally.

passkeys.description:
The server can register and sign in with passkeys: it has a public address WebAuthn accepts (a host name over
https, or localhost). Without it, only authenticator apps are offered.

revision.description: The commit the server binary was built from; null when the build did not record one.

version.description: The server's release version; empty when an older server did not report one.

ServerInvitationGrant.description: The role a server invitation gives in one repository or one organization; exactly one of the two targets.

ServerInvitationInfo.description: A server invitation as an administrator sees it; the code is never part of it.

created_by.description: The server administrator who created it.

expires_at.description: When set and not in the future, the credential is expired: refused, but still listed.

last_used_from.description: The address of the last accepted request; absent when the server could not tell.

rate_limit_per_minute.description: The credential's own limit in requests per minute; absent means the server default.

csrf_token.description: Send as the `X-Pyn-CSRF` header on every POST, PUT and DELETE.

password_change_required.description:
True when an administrator set the password and the person must replace it (`PUT /v1/me/password`).
Advisory: the server does not refuse other requests until it is changed.

SetLimitsRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are; a number sets the limit and `null` returns the field to the server default.

members.description: Organizations only; a user has no member limit.

SetOrgSettingsRequest.description: Replaces the organization's settings: a field left out or null is cleared.

SetRepoStorageCapRequest.description: The new storage cap of a repository; `null` removes it.

grace_days.description:
0 to 90 days, default 7. Setting the same requirement again changes nothing; a different grace period starts
the clock again.

user.description: The first administrator, who can now sign in with the password.

oneOf.description: Omit it to take the server's configured default (`PYN_ACCESS`, else `private`).

public_url.description: The address people reach the web app at; verification links use it.

token.description: The one-time setup token printed by the server on first run (stderr) or from its `PYN_SETUP_TOKEN` setting.

SetupStatus.description: Whether first-run setup has happened; carries no secrets.

access_mode.description: What setup recorded or an administrator set later; before setup, the configured default.

public_url.description: What setup recorded; before setup, the address the server is configured with.

registration.description: What setup recorded, or the configured default before setup.

server_name.description: Set once setup recorded a name.

SignInOptions.description: How people can sign in to this server.

oneOf.description: The configured external provider; null when the server has none.

passkeys.description:
Whether a passkey can sign in (`POST /v1/session/passkey/begin`); false when the server has no public address
WebAuthn accepts.

password.description: Whether anyone may sign in with a password. When false, server administrators still can.

SnapshotEntry.description: A path as of a commit: the revision the commit's ancestry gives it. `mode` is what `.pyn/pyn.toml` says at that commit.

content.description: The content's git blob id at that revision.

SnapshotPage.description: The whole repository as of one commit.

commit.description: The id of the commit the entries are as of; null for a repository with no commits.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

StarState.description: A repository's star count and whether the caller starred it.

StarredRepo.description: One repository in an account's list of stars.

StartAccessSessionRequest.description: Starts an access session on the account named in the path.

notes.description: Required for `other`, at most 500 characters. The account sees them.

reason.description: One of `abuse_report`, `security_incident`, `support_request`, `legal_request` or `other`; chosen for each session.

StartedAccessSession.description: A started session. The secret is the credential the administrator presents as a bearer token.

StorageSettings.description: Where file content is kept (`PYN_S3_BUCKET`, `PYN_DATA_DIR` or neither) and whether it answered the last check.

bucket.description: The bucket name for `s3`; null otherwise. The endpoint and the credentials are never reported.

status.description: `degraded` when the store failed its last probe (an S3 store is probed about every 30 seconds).

StrandedVersion.description:
A shared version a branch holds of a path that became exclusive on the default branch (decision #38). It stays in
history but can no longer merge into the path's single line.

author_current.description: The author's name now, when it differs from `author` (decision #986).

oneOf.description: The author's public identity (the current name's account when renamed); absent when no active account holds it.

branch.description: The branch that holds the version.

branch_owner.description: Who created the branch; the audit log tells them (`version_stranded`).

commit.description: The commit the revision belongs to.

conversion.description: The conversion revision the default branch made when the path became exclusive; absent in a preview.

revision.description: The stranded revision of the path.

Tag.description: A tag: an immutable name pointing at a commit. It never moves; deleting it frees the name.

commit.description: The commit the tag points at.

committed_at.description: The committed time of the tagged commit.

message.description: The note given when the tag was made; null when there was none.

TeamInfo.description: A team of an organization with its members and repository roles.

id.description: Stable id: never changes and is never issued again after a delete, so key data on it, not the slug.

TeamRepo.description: A repository where a team holds a role.

expires_at.description: Absent means the token never expires.

sign_in.description: Issued by `pyn login`: a full-scope credential rather than a fine-grained token.

user.description: The account that created the token and whose role it is capped by.

TokenPermission.description: One permission of a fine-grained token: a resource at a level.

level.description:
`read` or `write` (write includes read); `admin` for `locks` only (includes write). `org_audit` and
`account_locks` take `read` only.

resource.description:
Repository permissions: `metadata`, `contents`, `locks`, `policy`, `members`, `administration` or `audit`.
Organization permissions, for an organization owner: `org_members`, `org_teams`, `org_administration` or
`org_audit`. Account permissions, for the caller's own account as owner: `account_profile`,
`account_ssh_keys` or `account_locks`.

TotpConfirmed.description: A factor that is now on.

recovery_codes.description: Ten single-use recovery codes, shown only now, and only with the account's first factor.

TotpEnrolment.description: A pending authenticator-app enrolment. The seed is shown once; the factor counts only after `confirm`.

secret.description: The seed in base32, for typing into an app.

uri.description: The `otpauth://` URI to show as a QR code.

oneOf.description: The newest revision at or under the entry (`path` on it names the file). Absent for a file with a lock but no revision.
The live lock on a file; always absent for folders.

path.description: Repo-relative path; pass it as `path` to list a folder.

entries.description: Folders first, then files, each by name.

path.description: The listed folder; empty for the root.

TwoFactorFactor.description: A second factor the account has turned on.

TwoFactorRequired.description: A requirement that the account hold a second factor, and what happens at the deadline.

by.description: `server` (an administrator requires it of everyone) or `organization`.

deadline.description: From this moment the account can only set up a second factor (`403 two_factor_enrolment_required`).

enforced.description: True once the deadline has passed.

organization.description: The organization that requires it, when `by` is `organization`.

TwoFactorSetting.description: Whether second factors are required, and the grace period.

grace_days.description: Days an account without a factor keeps full access after `since` (or after it was created).

since.description: When the requirement was set; absent when none is.

enabled.description: Whether the account has a confirmed factor or a passkey, so sign-in asks for a second step.

passkeys.description: Passkeys and security keys; each one also counts as a second factor, so `enabled` is true when there is one.

passkeys_available.description: Whether this server can register passkeys (see `ServerCapabilities.passkeys`).

oneOf.description: What still requires the account to enrol (see `Account.two_factor_required`).

UpdateOrgProfileRequest.description: The organization profile text; each field that is blank or left out is cleared.

url.description: http or https only, at most 200 characters, no user name or password.

UpdateProfileRequest.description: The new profile text: every field is replaced, and one left out or blank is cleared.

oneOf.description: Left out, the stored visibility is kept; given, it replaces it (a field missing from it is visible).

UpdateRepoRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are.

allow_private_forks.description: Whether people who can read the repository may fork it while it is private.

description.description: One line, at most 350 characters; `null` or blank clears it.

max_locks_per_user.description: A number sets the limit, `null` returns to the server default. Refused while the policy file sets one.

name.description: The new name, normalised like a new repository's.

topics.description: Replaces every topic; `[]` removes them all.

oneOf.description: Changing it needs the owner with admin rights and is recorded in the audit log.

website.description: An http or https link; `null` or blank clears it.

UpdateStatus.description: Whether a newer pyn release exists, as this server last learned it (`GET /v1/admin/update`).

checked_at.description: When the last successful lookup finished; absent while none has. With `latest` absent, present means up to date.

enabled.description: The server runs the check (`PYN_UPDATE_CHECK=on`). When false, every other field but `current` is absent.

latest.description: The newest release on this server's channel; absent when the server is up to date or has not learned it yet.

prerelease.description: Whether `latest` is a pre-release; present with `latest`.

UpdateTeamRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are.

UpdateWebhookRequest.description: Fields left out stay as they are.

event_types.description: Replaces the list; an empty list means every type. An unknown type is refused with `400 invalid_request`.

lfs_bytes.description: Bytes of LFS objects. The storage limit applies to `stored_bytes` plus this.

members.description: Organization members; null for a user.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes of distinct revision content, counted once per repository.

token.description: The token from the verification link.

VerifyProblem.description:
One break found by verification: `hash_mismatch` (a record's fields do not give its hash), `version_mismatch` (a revision's `hash_version` disagrees with its stored fields), `broken_link` (it does
not follow the record before it) `base_mismatch` (a revision's base is not an older revision of its path) or `pointer_mismatch` (a commit's pointer cache differs from the revisions it made and adopted). Revision breaks carry `path` and `revision`; audit breaks carry `event`.

commit.description: The commit id, for a problem in a commit record.

VerifyReport.description:
What one `verify` request checked. With `paged=true` a request does a bounded share of the work: add the counts and
problems of the steps together, and send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` until it is null.

audit_events.description: Events checked; null when the audit log was not checked (a single path, or no `view_audit`).

next_cursor.description:
Opaque; send it as `cursor` for the next step. Null when everything has been checked. Absent from servers that
check in one request.

Visibility.description: Public: anyone, signed in or not, may read the repository. Private: members only, and everyone else gets 404.

WatchLevel.description: What a watcher hears about: every event of the repository, only its lock events, or nothing at all.

WatchState.description: The caller's watch level on a repository and how many accounts watch it.

oneOf.description: Null when the caller chose no level.

WatchedRepo.description: One repository in the caller's list of watched repositories.

updated_at.description: When the level was last set.

event_types.description: Event types delivered; empty means every type.

secrets.description: Active secrets, oldest first: one, or two while a rotation is in progress.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event's delivery to one subscription. The `id` is the `Pyn-Delivery` header and stays the same across retries and redeliveries.

attempts.description: Attempts made since the last queueing or redelivery.

event_id.description: The queued event's id; the paging cursor.

last_status_code.description: The receiver's status code on the last attempt, if it answered.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due; meaningful while pending.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next, older page; null on the last page.

WebhookEventTypeInfo.description: One event type a webhook subscription may list.

description.description: One line saying when it is raised.

WebhookSecretInfo.description: An active signing secret. Its value is shown once, when it is created, and never again.

encrypted.description: Whether the server stores it encrypted (`PYN_SECRET_KEY` is set).
